items.title: Normalize optimization suggestions
items.problem: Daily reports recorded follow-up suggestions with multiple incompatible field shapes, so future sessions could not reliably consume them.
items.expected_behavior: New report writes normalize `self_check.optimization_suggestions` to one canonical field contract, and arbitrary objects fail schema validation.

validation.test_name: schema rejects arbitrary optimization_suggestions objects

items.title: Require ledger-backed feedback gates
items.problem: User-confirmed feedback could be written as advice without becoming a durable test or gate.
items.expected_behavior: Every open P1 feedback ledger item includes existing scope files, a validation command covered by `pnpm run validate`, and a test name that exists in `tests/**`.

validation.test_name: feedback contract requires P1 ledger items to bind to tests or gates

items.title: Prove latest origin/main baseline
items.problem: A merged PR could fail to affect new sessions if generation starts from stale local `main` instead of the latest `origin/main`.
items.expected_behavior: `report:write` records `origin_main_sha`, and strict publish quality blocks reports whose generation commit does not match current `origin/main`.

validation.test_name: publish quality blocks strict daily reports not generated from current origin/main

items.title: Use a clean publish checkout for scheduled runs
items.problem: Scheduled daily runs could start from a feature branch, detached HEAD, dirty launcher worktree, or unavailable current `.git` metadata, causing generation or publish to fail after content was already prepared.
items.expected_behavior: Scheduled daily runs first prepare a dedicated clean checkout from current `origin/main`, switch to `prepared.next_cwd`, and run generation, validation, date-scoped dry-run, and publish there without committing, stashing, switching, or cleaning the launcher worktree.

validation.test_name: publish prepare-clean-worktree clones a dedicated main checkout without touching launcher changes

items.title: Expose source discovery outages
items.problem: A scheduled run could have most fixed sources blocked while old populated sections made the public report look healthy.
items.expected_behavior: When multiple fixed source groups are mostly blocked with network-like errors, the report records `source_discovery_network_unavailable`, exposes blocked counts, and tells the user to check Codex network access for workspace-write sandbox mode.

validation.test_name: publish quality exposes network-wide source outage even when sections are populated

items.title: Keep fixed sources and open metadata effective
items.problem: Requested RSS/API/aggregator sources could be present in registries and source_audit but fail to affect daily selection because early feeds consumed the global discovery candidate limit; configured source_level values could also pass registry validation and then fail only after the candidate artifact reached report_write.
items.expected_behavior: Content discovery visits the full enabled source surface, records every source in source_audit, and fairly preserves later fixed-source results under transport limits. Source-level and classification fields are open metadata: new non-empty values survive registry, candidate, report, and occurrence boundaries, while canonical public labels use an explicit fallback. The draft producer persists the lossless occurrence store before editorial selection and separately validates the legacy editorial pool before writing or authoring.

validation.test_name: registry rejects retired source classification while candidate and report schemas keep legacy read compatibility

items.title: Preserve partial search discovery
items.problem: `discover:search-news` could obscure provider-level failures and did not record provider timing or error counts.
items.expected_behavior: Shadow search keeps candidates from healthy providers when another provider fails, and records provider runtime, request cost, and error counts in `source_audit.search_sources`.

validation.test_name: search transport page size limits each request without capping aggregate listener output

items.title: Write clean discovery JSON
items.problem: Saving discovery stdout through PowerShell could be polluted by encoding, BOM, or npm banners.
items.expected_behavior: JSON-producing CLI commands accept `--output` and write clean UTF-8 JSON files directly while avoiding accidental argument inference from output file paths.

validation.test_name: CLI JSON commands can write clean UTF-8 output files

items.title: Keep generic watch-next metadata out of visible main bullets
items.problem: The pre-rendered daily report surfaced generic `watch_next` and `why_it_matters` metadata as repeated visible bullets such as `继续跟踪客户案例、官方后续数据和多源验证。` after main items.
items.expected_behavior: Main-item visible bullets render factual bullets, reader relevance, and explicit non-primary verification/risk notes only; generic `why_it_matters` and `watch_next` metadata remains in structured JSON and does not appear as repeated prose in the main section.

validation.test_name: 日报可以转换为 effective-interact 输入

items.title: Promote main item groups into first-level navigation
items.problem: The public report used a parent `主体信息` section with child headings, making navigation noisy and hiding the actual main-topic groups.
items.expected_behavior: The public report does not render `主体信息` as a top-level section or navigation item; main-item groups render as first-level navigation sections with concise labels such as `AI 资讯`, `大厂与政策`, and `产品与开源`.

validation.test_name: 日报可以转换为 effective-interact 输入

items.title: Keep domestic observations visible across public monitoring
items.problem: Domestic Chinese AI dynamics could be present in the candidate pool but remain buried in source audit or mixed community leads, making the public report look dominated by overseas vendor updates.
items.expected_behavior: Every safely normalized Chinese or domestic observation enters the public signal stream under its source group, including community clues, with content and credibility labels instead of qualification gates. Inside the optional legacy edited report only, unresolved high-risk intermediary claims are not promoted to factual main stories and the old `community_leads` section remains non-public.

validation.test_name: repository contract keeps public signal membership lossless and labels non-gating

items.title: Run AI-ready quality review before publish
items.problem: Daily drafts could pass structural gates while still retaining AI-flavored wording, automatic draft template prose, noisy highlights, thin bullets, Builder translation drift, or unchecked candidate-pool back-references.
items.expected_behavior: The optional legacy edited-report pipeline reviews draft JSON against its candidate pool before report:write, exposes current matching issue.details to bounded repair, permits contracts only for unresolved legacy paths, continues only after strict blocking-signal reduction, rolls back the first stalled attempt, and suppresses content-contract re-entry before its targeted page checklist. These quality gates never control occurrence persistence, docs/signals membership, chronology, or publication.

validation.test_name: daily runner rolls back a stalled repair and suppresses content-contract re-entry

items.title: Public daily content is compact news, not explanations
items.problem: The public daily report could render too few real main stories while spending visible space on selection rationale, watch-next advice, source-type grids, and other AI-flavored filler instead of concise source-backed news.
items.expected_behavior: This contract remains applicable to the legacy edited-report artifact only. The controlling public product direction changed on 2026-07-14: the site is a source-first signal listener, not an 8-12-story admission surface. Public signal cards expose concise reader-safe summaries, links, publisher/collector separation, source group, content tags, and credibility tags; editorial rationale, candidate scores, rejection reasons, and internal audit fields remain private.

validation.test_name: public daily contract accepts no-image short news without explanation fields

items.title: Refill sparse main stream from a blacklist-filtered unified pool
items.problem: The daily generator treated `main_items` as an official/primary whitelist pool, so days with many usable GitHub, Builder, blog, community, and weak-signal candidates could still publish only a few main stories; later patches then tried to compensate with hard post-generation gates and public filler.
items.expected_behavior: This confirmed requirement is now scoped only to the optional legacy edited-report summary. Its blacklist, qualification, refill, 5-item minimum, ranking, dedupe, and rejection audit may choose summary stories, but none of those values or decisions may remove, demote, or reorder records in the public source signal stream governed by feedback/p1-lossless-public-signal-stream.

validation.test_name: report:draft fills sparse main stream from unified candidate roles

items.title: Public media must be readable content assets
items.problem: The public page used full-page browser screenshots as main evidence for public leaderboards and rendered tiny icons, favicons, logos, or unreadable images as article media.
items.expected_behavior: Full-page screenshots, browser viewport captures, icons, favicons, logos, avatars, undersized images, and unreadable media do not render as public正文 content. No-image reports can still pass. OpenRouter, Artificial Analysis, and similar public pages prefer parsed DOM/JSON/text tables with ranks, models, providers, scores/tokens, and changes.

validation.test_name: public daily contract rejects invalid public media but allows missing media

items.title: Require semantic public evidence images
items.problem: Daily reports could publish decorative article images, hero art, generic stock-like pictures, logos, favicons, avatars, or generic computer pictures as正文 evidence even when the source article contained meaningful benchmark tables, charts, architecture diagrams, or product screenshots.
items.expected_behavior: Public evidence assets are allowed only when they carry article-specific information such as benchmark, leaderboard, table, chart, diagram, architecture, or product screenshot content. Decorative image candidates are filtered before caching and rejected by strict publish quality if they remain in the report JSON.

validation.test_name: semantic evidence asset gate rejects decorative article images

items.title: Run the China AI source lane and disclose collection outages
items.problem: Domestic Chinese AI sources could be absent because daily discovery did not have an explicit China AI lane and successful publish quality did not distinguish an executed-but-empty China lane from a lane that never ran.
items.expected_behavior: For the optional legacy edited report dated 2026-06-11 or later, strict report publication requires `source_audit.china_ai_sources` with checked source proof. The public listener records lane failure as source-health/access metadata and still publishes every occurrence collected from healthy lanes; missing execution or no qualified legacy story must never delete, delay, or reorder those observations.

validation.test_name: china ai hard gate blocks strict publish when China lane is missing

items.title: Render tracking sources as structured visual tables
items.problem: OpenRouter, Artificial Analysis, and similar ranking sources could appear as plain text icons or screenshots instead of source-like ranked tables that preserve model, provider, score, usage, cost, and change signals.
items.expected_behavior: Tracking sources with structured rows render as compact public tables or leaderboard components. Full-page screenshots are not accepted as the primary public carrier; screenshots may only be cropped table evidence and remain lower priority than parsed DOM, JSON, or text data.

validation.test_name: tracking visual components render OpenRouter and Artificial Analysis without screenshots or summary log cards

items.title: Preserve Chinese AI blogs in monitoring and legacy summaries
items.problem: The `hot_blogs` section could be entirely overseas and English even when qualified Chinese or China AI technical blog candidates were available.
items.expected_behavior: Every safely normalized Chinese or China AI blog observation enters the public signal stream without qualification or slot limits. Inside the optional legacy edited report only, selection reserves visible `hot_blogs` coverage for at least one qualified candidate or records an explicit reason; those factual gates cannot affect public membership or chronology.

validation.test_name: report:draft reserves Chinese hot blog slot when qualified

items.title: Add Hugging Face Trending discovery and public monitoring
items.problem: The report had GitHub Trending but no equivalent Hugging Face Trending lane, so model, dataset, and Space trend signals were not independently discovered or displayed.
items.expected_behavior: Daily discovery runs Hugging Face Trending and stores auditable source metadata. Every safe model, dataset, and Space observation enters the public `papers_models` signal group; the old `huggingface_trending` Top 10 is only a legacy edited-report projection and cannot cap or qualify the public stream.

validation.test_name: huggingface trending discovery and public section

items.title: Keep X/Twitter discussion cards compact
items.problem: Builder and X/Twitter discussion cards could leave excessive whitespace, translate or paraphrase original posts into generic commentary, or expose internal source-bucket labels.
items.expected_behavior: The pre-cutover runtime keeps author, handle, date, source link, and original post text when available without exposing internal fields. The accepted target replaces generic Builder cards with the typed X contract in the atomic PR6 cutover; the old no-tag compact-card rule remains legacy-only until then. PR3 performs source/raw/funnel shadow work and does not remove a public surface.

validation.test_name: public X signals preserve author handle and original post text

items.title: Superseded public source coverage visualization
items.problem: The public `source coverage and gaps` section regressed into a dense text list, hiding the actual visit status, gaps, and source-lane health from readers.
items.expected_behavior: Superseded on 2026-07-01 by the public surface diet: public daily pages no longer render source coverage/gaps. Source health and coverage details stay in internal diagnostics only.

validation.test_name: public source coverage visualization is retired from public daily reports

items.title: Separate reader report from internal quality report
items.problem: Reader-facing daily pages exposed source audit appendices, self-check output, degradation logs, candidate/inclusion diagnostics, and other internal publishing mechanics as if they were article content.
items.expected_behavior: Public daily HTML hides internal audit/debug/quality sections by default. Internal sections are available only through explicit internal report options or JSON artifacts, while public pages keep the reader-focused sections and source links.

validation.test_name: public daily contract renders structured tracking components instead of screenshots and hides audit appendices

items.title: Keep public daily from becoming a machine audit log
items.problem: The public daily can regress from a reader-facing story report into dense machine audit output: source health logs, fetch/retry notes, candidate pool diagnostics, parsed counters, ledger notes, or regression self-check text appearing as public content.
items.expected_behavior: Public pages stay source-first and reader-facing. Reader-safe publisher/collector attribution, source/content/credibility labels, health/access state, summaries, and links may be visible; raw source_audit, sources_health, candidate_pool, fetch/retry logs, parsed_count, notes fields, ledger review, regression self-check, and machine execution details remain internal-only.

validation.test_name: public daily rejects machine audit logs from reader-facing sections

items.title: Rank the optional edited report by public AI importance
items.problem: Selection rules could suppress broad AI news, official product updates, big-company moves, and general AI热点 because they were not directly tied to the user's immediate work.
items.expected_behavior: Inside the optional legacy edited report only, candidate scoring gives explicit weight to broad public AI importance rather than personal relevance. The public signal stream ignores that score for membership and default order; the LLM may draft summaries but cannot create a hidden admission, count, media, or blocking policy.

validation.test_name: report:draft promotes official product and platform deep dives into main_items

items.title: Public docs data must not expose internal drafting state
items.problem: The public GitHub Pages data artifact under docs/data exposed internal fields such as candidate_id, source_audit, self_check, why_it_matters, reader_relevance, watch_next, and full candidate pools.
items.expected_behavior: Build output writes a reader-safe docs/data report that omits internal audit, self-check, candidate, scoring, rationale, source_effectiveness rows, source-level diagnostics, and publish-debug fields. Candidate pools stay in reports-data only and are not copied to public docs/data by default.

validation.test_name: buildSite writes reader-safe public data without internal fields or candidate pools

items.title: Superseded platform exempt discovery wiring

items.expected_behavior: Superseded on 2026-07-01. Daily generation no longer runs discover:wechat-platform, discover:zhihu-platform, or discover:reddit-platform. Direct Chinese RSS, GitHub watchlist, and community hotspots replace this lane.

validation.test_name: daily runner omits retired platform discovery outputs from report draft

items.title: Superseded platform exempt public rendering
items.problem: Low-threshold platform sections could technically work while still publishing internal discovery fields, machine-generated feed titles, or long English excerpts as reader content.

validation.test_name: public daily omits source coverage gaps and retired platform diagnostics

items.title: Replay the 2026-06-09 bad public daily

items.expected_behavior: A fixture replay of the 2026-06-09 failure triggers main-density and media-contract issues, renders leaderboard data as a table instead of screenshot media, and keeps internal audit/debug text out of public interaction input.

validation.test_name: public daily contract replays 2026-06-09 bad media and short-main regression

items.title: Require feedback memory review and regression self-check
items.problem: User-reported issues could be fixed once but future task specs did not force Codex to review the feedback ledger or record an explicit regression self-check.
items.expected_behavior: Every repository modification records a meaningful `Feedback Ledger Review` and `Regression Self-Check`; harness validation fails when either section is missing or empty, and the quick reference plus `docs/ai-daily-requirements-reconciliation.md` summarize durable requirements, ledger links, tests, and runtime evidence boundaries.

validation.test_name: feedback memory self-check rejects quick reference missing ledger item

items.title: Map durable ai-daily requirements to runtime evidence
items.problem: The user repeatedly confirmed ai-daily requirements, but prior fixes could mark items implemented without proving that the generated daily report, index page, tests, and runtime evidence actually satisfied them.
items.expected_behavior: Every durable ai-daily requirement is listed in `docs/ai-daily-requirements-reconciliation.md` with a requirement ID, linked feedback ledger item, test or gate, runtime evidence boundary, and current implementation status. Cross-agent Codex/Claude Code diagnosis that changes implementation priority is promoted into a repository roadmap before downstream work is claimed accepted. The repo must not claim a requirement is stable unless the handoff cites generated artifacts and validation evidence.

validation.test_name: ai daily requirements reconciliation maps user requirements to ledger tests and runtime evidence

items.title: Publish the broad signal stream with uncertainty labels, not qualification gates
items.problem: Daily report safety gates could be too strict, then the attempted fix made qualified third-party reports, builder posts, blogs, and community leads readable only through repetitive generic labels such as 来源/第三方报道/社区线索.
items.expected_behavior: Superseded for the public product on 2026-07-14 by feedback/p1-lossless-public-signal-stream. All safely normalizable official, third-party, builder, GitHub, media, and community occurrences enter the public source stream without qualification gates or section caps. Source level and verification metadata remain labels only. The old strict/capped behavior is retained solely for the legacy editorial report artifact and must never control public signal membership or default chronology.

validation.test_name: repository contract keeps public signal membership lossless and labels non-gating

items.title: Preserve legacy editorial importance without narrowing public monitoring
items.problem: Daily reports could miss the original model launch, split channel availability into separate main stories, render one-line hot blog summaries, recycle low-utility vendor PR, and lose source-gap evidence entirely.
items.expected_behavior: Inside the optional legacy edited report, original model/provider launches outrank duplicate channel availability, duplicate story context may be folded together, and hot blogs use concrete summaries. The public signal stream still retains every safe duplicate observation and low-utility vendor item in chronology with visible labels. Raw source-gap diagnostics stay internal; compact reader-safe source health may never become admission or rank.

validation.test_name: report:draft promotes original Anthropic Fable/Mythos launch over platform availability duplicates

items.title: Resolve public link icons deterministically
items.problem: Public report cards could fall back to first-letter generated icons even for known domains, making source identity look broken or inconsistent.
items.expected_behavior: All public links go through a unified resolver: explicit icon, unified GitHub icon for GitHub URLs, cached source/domain icon, and only then recorded generated initials fallback.

validation.test_name: icon resolver uses link domain icons and records fallback metadata

items.title: Enrich GitHub Trending from README
items.problem: GitHub Trending cards could describe repositories with one shallow sentence, duplicate tag text, or no useful explanation of the project's core README content.
items.expected_behavior: GitHub Trending descriptions prefer cached README-level Chinese summaries keyed by repo, branch, and sha; summaries explain capability, use case, and maturity signals while remaining bounded.

validation.test_name: GitHub Trending enriches descriptions from cached README summaries

items.title: Publish Chinese media dynamics
items.problem: Machine Heart, QbitAI, and SSPAI updates could be absent or reduced to a tiny slot, even when users wanted all in-window Chinese media dynamics summarized.
items.expected_behavior: QbitAI and SSPAI use direct RSS and Machine Heart uses a non-RSS HTML/API-style entry; every safe in-window observation remains in the pre-cutover source-grouped runtime. The independent Chinese-media section and roughly 200-character summaries apply only to the optional legacy rendered report, which remains current runtime until the atomic PR6 cutover. PR3 performs shadow source work only.

validation.test_name: Chinese media dynamics include all in-window QbitAI SSPAI and Machine Heart entries

items.title: Separate official organization updates
items.problem: Official lab/company/product updates could be mixed into Builder/X discussion, making official organization signals hard to scan.
items.expected_behavior: Official organization observations enter the pre-cutover public official_blogs source group and remain distinct from personal X observations through source metadata. The old dedicated official-updates section applies only to the optional legacy rendered report and remains current runtime until its information is migrated and its route retired atomically in PR6; PR3 does not change public routes.

validation.test_name: official organization updates render separately from Builder observations

items.title: Retire unconfigured platform source degradation
items.problem: WeChat or Zhihu without a real configured entrypoint used to require explicit degraded quality reasons, but the platform lanes are now retired from the default workflow.
items.expected_behavior: Legacy WeChat/Zhihu source_audit fields may remain in old internal fixtures, but they do not create public degraded reasons, affected sections, or blocking issues. New durable coverage comes from the GitHub watchlist, direct Chinese RSS, and community hotspots.

validation.test_name: retired WeChat and Zhihu source audit fields do not create public degradation

items.title: Rebuild tracking components locally
items.problem: OpenRouter and Artificial Analysis tracking could regress to screenshots, plain text tables, or opaque raw-page dumps instead of local interactive components with traceable source data.
items.expected_behavior: Daily tracking items emit `tracking_component_snapshot` with normalized tabs, series, rows, hashes, fallback reasons, and public trace; source snapshots preserve OpenRouter weekly history and Artificial Analysis score/token/cost/scatter tab data when collected; the public page renders local tabs, linear/log controls, hover data, stacked/history rows, and trace without third-party runtime JS or raw DOM exposure.

validation.test_name: collectContentSources stores Artificial Analysis token cost and scatter tabs

items.title: Superseded must-read hero requirement
items.problem: The former three-card must-read contract is no longer the public daily target and would now force an obsolete first-screen layout.
items.expected_behavior: Historical and closed: the 2026-06-23 hero contract and the 2026-07-14 source-group replacement plan are both superseded by the 2026-07-15 curated-edition target. The obsolete hero/report route remains current runtime until the atomic PR6 cutover, which replaces it with the globally ranked warm-paper edition; PR3 does not change public routes.

validation.test_name: interaction input starts with story-first judgment trends and story list

items.title: Keep public reader sections concrete and dense
items.problem: Public AI daily pages could duplicate the main stream with a `完整列表`, leave main details collapsed, show GitHub Trending rows with generic ranking/README boilerplate, render blank or broken X/Twitter cards when optional fields were missing, and reduce community leads to one-line blurbs.
items.expected_behavior: This remains a legacy edited-report rendering contract until the atomic PR6 cutover. The accepted replacement is a globally ranked curated edition plus typed GitHub/X/Paper/Model/Benchmark semantics and a separate clean /signals pool, all without internal review notes or machine audit fields. PR3 performs shadow source work only.

validation.test_name: public daily renders story-first sections without compact full list

items.title: Reset public daily IA and source effectiveness gates
items.problem: The public daily could still be technically generated while showing low-density sections, generic explanatory filler, translated X/Twitter commentary, table-like daily tracking regressions, hover-dim interactions, and no clear answer for whether each core source was configured, reachable, parsed, selected as candidate, and publicly included.
items.expected_behavior: Superseded for the public IA on 2026-07-14 by the source-first signal stream. Public pages group all safely normalizable occurrences by source attributes, keep GitHub, X, community, media/newsletter, official-blog, and paper/model groups independently browsable, and use credibility/content/source metadata only as visible filters. Raw source-effectiveness diagnostics, internal audit fields, scores, and rejection reasons remain private; source health may appear only as a compact record label and never as admission or default ranking input.

validation.test_name: public daily IA reset enforces stories original X compact tracking hover and source effectiveness

items.title: Keep production daily HTML on effective-interact
items.problem: A remediation attempted to remove public-page garbage by replacing the production daily report renderer with a bespoke public template that carried fake `data-html-work-report` and `data-render-mode` markers, losing effective-interact components and historical validation requirements.
items.expected_behavior: Until the atomic PR6 cutover retires the old rendered daily pages, the optional legacy single-report HTML is generated through `.codex/skills/effective-interact/scripts/create-interaction.mjs` in `pre-rendered` mode and retains its historical renderer checks. This is a legacy compatibility contract, not authority for the accepted curated React application; PR3 performs shadow source work only.

validation.test_name: buildSite writes reader-safe public JSON for 2026-06-15 without internal leakage

items.title: Recover public editorial repair failures with ready-gated templates
items.problem: A quality repair contract could apply every edit but still fail the post-repair review on public-copy wording, leaving the runner blocked at `quality_ai_repair` even though the failure was recoverable with a second editorial pass.
items.expected_behavior: Only post-repair failures limited to public editorial AI review tasks and zero rejected edits may return to `needs_ai_repair`; the runner writes a new empty contract template with `status:"template"`, `edits:[]`, review issue summaries, and bad-example comments, and it never executes that template until it is changed to `status:"ready"` with at least one edit. validation.test_name: daily runner creates a new empty AI repair template for public editorial repair failures

items.title: Gate daily content quality before publish
items.problem: The 2026-06-17 run exposed weak generated content that structural checks did not reject: one-bullet main details, filler-heavy hot blog text, shallow GitHub Trending descriptions, zero Builder/X selections despite enough eligible X feed candidates, and fake simplified tracking components.
items.expected_behavior: The deterministic content-contract checker remains a gate for the legacy edited-report artifact and reconstructed tracking components. validation.test_name: real artifact content contract scans report JSON and surfaces blocking issues

items.title: Reject full-page official tracking snapshots

validation.test_name: daily tracking broad official snapshots degrade instead of rendering full-page dumps

items.title: Prune duplicate or templated public items before repair

validation.test_name: report:draft prunes duplicate and templated hot blogs before quality review

items.title: Generate the daily main list as deduped edited stories

items.expected_behavior: This remains implemented for the legacy edited-report artifact, where the generator builds a deduped story list and GitHub module. validation.test_name: story-centered daily contract is implemented with generator and rendering gates

items.title: Keep authoritative sanitized retrospectives in the repository
items.problem: Task blockers, iteration advice, and daily publish lessons could remain only in chat, local task state, or raw automation logs, making them hard to reuse safely in future runs.
items.expected_behavior: Non-trivial deliveries and daily publish runs write sanitized retrospective records with explicit run_type and suggestion status, keep one lightweight committed index, finalize publish-mode records before real publish, append selected-date rollup corrections when publish and fallback both fail, and reject private paths, secrets, raw logs, index drift, and implemented suggestions without durable evidence.

validation.test_name: daily runner writes sanitized daily publish retrospective before validation

items.title: Publish daily tracking source outages as degraded
items.problem: Artificial Analysis or similar daily tracking sources can have official snapshot collection failures. items.expected_behavior: `daily_tracking` items may carry `source_unavailable_note` when the official component snapshot is unavailable. validation.test_name: report:write accepts source-unavailable daily tracking as degraded

items.title: Keep daily publish recovery policy executable
items.problem: Recent scheduled daily runs failed for different causes because retry, fallback, degradation, and blocking behavior were scattered across runner code, prompts, runbooks, and automation expectations instead of being checked as one workflow contract.
items.expected_behavior: The repository keeps `config/daily-resilience-policy.json` as the authoritative retry/fallback/degrade/block table for the current legacy edited-report runner stages. Validation proves those stages and terminal taxonomies are covered. This policy may block unsafe legacy content or rendering but must not make a failed edited report block the independent docs/signals publication path introduced by PR2.

validation.test_name: daily resilience policy validates current runner stages and workflow gates

items.title: Preserve public daily follow-up quality contracts
items.problem: Public daily pages can regress after IA changes: Artificial Analysis can expose empty score/cost/scatter tabs, story labels can use awkward bilingual wording or repeat `披露`, external links can stay in the same tab, GitHub Trending can show template README summaries, X/Twitter avatars can fail to localize, and platform/GitHub-watch source lanes can look ineffective or be misattributed.
items.expected_behavior: Daily public reports hide uncollected Artificial Analysis tabs instead of rendering empty fallback panels; the story list is titled `今日主线`; story titles avoid repeated `披露`; every external report link opens a new tab with `noopener noreferrer`; GitHub Trending rejects `README 主要围绕`/`阅读时先看` template summaries and falls back to source/rank/star facts; Builder/X cards infer downloaded local avatars from `avatar_url`; internal source effectiveness includes explicit GitHub watchlist, Chinese direct RSS, community hotspots, and GitHub organization-watch rows and does not attribute GitHub Trending weekly candidates to RuanYF Weekly; public output uses source links and reader-facing tracking without exposing public `source_effectiveness` rows.

validation.test_name: public daily followups hide empty Artificial Analysis fallback tabs

items.title: Keep the public daily slim and bind the new source reset
items.problem: The user repeatedly requested that public pages stop showing machine-audit/log wording and that new source requirements land durably, but prior iterations left old platform lanes, public source coverage, weak GitHub watch wiring, and AI-flavored public copy able to recur.
items.expected_behavior: Public pages remain reader-facing and must not expose raw source_audit, source_effectiveness tables, candidate pools, repair state, scores, or machine logs. The 2026-07-14 direction reset intentionally restores source-first information architecture through safe occurrence cards, publisher/collector attribution, tags, and source-group navigation rather than an operational dashboard. GitHub watchlist, direct Chinese RSS, community hotspots, and future public/legal collectors may all contribute occurrences without a whitelist or qualification gate.

validation.test_name: registered listener sources cover broader tech, official changelogs, and community feeds

items.title: Keep daily generation split into debuggable MVP stages
items.problem: The generated daily report can pass structure while publishing source-first machine logs as reader copy, mixing admission rationale into summaries, default-folding each story into an overdesigned detail panel, flattening left-rail hierarchy, and regressing icon/tag/type scale.
items.expected_behavior: Legacy edited-report generation keeps collection, optional story selection, per-item summary, and assembly independently debuggable. The public source stream branches immediately after collection, before that optional selection stage. Candidate scores, source audit, rejection reasons, and watch-next remain internal; reader-safe occurrence cards expose only concise summaries, links, attribution, source group, content tags, credibility tag, health, access, and time metadata.

validation.test_name: daily Codex DAG-lite runner plans the six MVP stages

items.title: Classify scheduled automations by explicit role
items.problem: Read-only insight automations can be misclassified as `status:self-check` jobs when their prompt mentions that command as context or a non-goal.
items.expected_behavior: Automation inventory uses explicit role metadata or a narrow allowlisted identity before prompt heuristics, so daily publish, status self-check, and read-only insight jobs are counted separately.

validation.test_name: automation inventory uses explicit readonly insight role

items.title: Preserve the lossless signal implementation as raw and legacy evidence
items.problem: The project repeatedly treated editorial selection, source authority, verification, qualification, quotas, dedupe, and quality review as public admission policy. That made the repository a small fact-summary page instead of the broad AI source listener the user requested, and old contracts could silently restore those gates even after the schema was relaxed.
items.expected_behavior: Closed as the default-homepage and new-pool target on 2026-07-15 by feedback/p1-curated-three-layer-homepage. Its implemented occurrence identity, raw lineage, URL safety, public-field privacy, atomic generation, baseline manifest and exact pre-cutover history remain required migration evidence. The phased migration must freeze that history as an immutable legacy archive and reuse raw observations as input, but it must not continue treating every safely normalized occurrence as new /signals or homepage membership.

validation.test_name: repository contract separates listener evidence from curated public surfaces

items.title: Separate raw listening, the persistent signal pool, and the curated homepage
items.problem: The lossless public occurrence stream made collection coverage equal public product value. The default homepage consequently exposed non-content endpoints, test rows, internal AI instructions, generic summaries, anonymous or indirect X search results, repeated benchmark rows, and specialized GitHub/paper/model data flattened into one generic card.
items.expected_behavior: The accepted target has three membership boundaries: internal repo-safe raw_observation, deterministic low-threshold admitted_signal, and high-threshold edition_item. Unclean material/quarantine is ignored and deleted within 24 hours; secrets never enter repository history. The default homepage is a globally ranked comprehensive AI edition: normal 10–14, honest short 5–9, and 0–4 preserves dated last-good as delayed/degraded; GitHub same-day Top10 is independent, X and papers/models each cap at 3 and may be zero. Every public item has a real content publisher/author and role, topic + format, public collector lineage and rounded identity icon. Ordinary generated copy is claim-span verified. Aify homepage Today Picks use a dedicated highest-priority trusted-upstream passthrough: the ordered title/description/link/tags become ready editorial content without summary, translation, editor, critic, semantic-verifier or scoring calls; Aify remains a distinct editorial source/collector, while the homepage shell and full articles.json archive never become Today Picks and can never be a silent fallback. All valid Today Picks enter the ready pool and prequalified candidate set, while the final edition still applies deterministic canonical/event, company, specialized-lane, diversity and 10–14 capacity constraints. Aify/newsletters/digests may separately publish a linked substantive article or act as collectors. The current warm-paper topbar/rail/two-column card language survives with A.D.C. as the only masthead copy, a hierarchical current-edition rail, Astryx primitives and @adc/design as sole token owner; no old lead/Today Five, inventory hero, or full-history search returns. /signals starts a clean post-cutover browsable pool; exact pre-cutover occurrences plus read-only legacy/unverified reports stay under /legacy. Asia/Shanghai cutoffs, immutable revisions and append-only corrections apply. GitHub/X/Paper/Model/Benchmark use typed contracts; every priority lane terminalizes, AI never decides admission, and no quota forces filler.

validation.test_name: repository contract separates listener evidence from curated public surfaces
